question: The income of Raman is ₹75400. He saves 23% of his income. If his income increases by 27% and expenditure increases by 50%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial income be 100%, then initial savings = 23% and initial expenditure = 77%.

New income = 100% + 27% = 127%.

New expenditure = 77% + (50% of 77%) = 77% × 1.50 = 115.5%.

New savings = 127% − 115.5% = 11.5%.

Decrease in savings = 23% − 11.5% = 11.5% of the initial income.

Decrease value = 11.5% of ₹75400 = (11.5 ÷ 100) × 75400 = ₹8671.

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹8671.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹75400

Initial Savings % = 23%

Income increase = 27%

Expenditure increase = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

 Original Income (100%)
 
 
 Exp 77%
 Sav 23%

 New Income (127%)
 
 
 New Exp 115.5%
 Sav 11.5%

 Decrease in Savings = 23% − 11.5% = 11.5% of Income

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Expenditure = (100% − 23%) of 75400 = 77% of 75400 = ₹58058

⇒ Initial Savings = 23% of 75400 = ₹17342

⇒ New Income = 75400 + (27% of 75400) = 75400 + 20358 = ₹95758

⇒ New Expenditure = 58058 + (50% of 58058) = 58058 + 29029 = ₹87087

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure = 95758 − 87087 = ₹8671

⇒ Change in Savings = Initial Savings − New Savings = 17342 − 8671 = ₹8671

⇒ Since New Savings [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income & Expenditure Concept

Income is always equal to the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Any percentage change in overall income gets distributed between expenditure and savings based on their respective initial values.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. If the calculation yields a negative result, it clearly indicates a percentage decrease.

Successive Percentage Changes

When a value changes by a% and then further changes by b%, the net effective percentage change is evaluated as a + b + (a × b)÷100. This is highly useful for multi-stage problems.
